angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 681,786 km at 68.00 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.7065 +/- 0.0159 mas (same row, RUWE 1.11): 68.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.98 +/- 0.007 solar radii from Egger et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HIP 29442 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.223E/abstract): 681,786 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.901 +/- 0.043 solar masses from Egger et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HIP 29442 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.223E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5289 +/- 69 K from Egger et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HIP 29442 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.223E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Egger et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HIP 29442 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.223E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hip-29442.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.410, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
